paragraphs.sourceText: Nursing, as a typically female profession, must deal constantly with the false impression that nurses are there to wait on the physician. As nurses, we are 26 to provide nursing care only. We do not have any legal or moral 27 any physician. We provide health teaching, assess physical as well as emotional problems, 28 patient-related services, and make all of our nursing decisions based upon what is best or suitable for the patient. If, in any circumstance, we feel that a physician’s order is inappropriate or unsafe, we have a legal 29 to question that order or refuse to carry it out.

Nursing is not a nine-to-five job with every weekend off. All nurses are aware of that before they enter the profession. The emotional and 30 stress, however, that occurs due to odd working hours is a 31 reason for a lot of the career dissatisfaction. It is sometimes required that we work overtime, and that we change shifts four or five times a month. That disturbs our personal lives, 32 our sleeping and eating habits, and isolates us from everything except job-related friends and activities.

The quality of nursing care is 33 dramatically by these situations. Most hospitals are now staffed by new graduates, as experienced nurses finally give up trying to change the system. Consumers of 34 related services have evidently not been affected enough yet to demand changes 35 . But if trends continue as predicted, they will find that most critical hospital care will be provided by new, inexperienced, and sometimes inadequately trained nurses. paragraphs.sourceText: Millions of Americans are entering their 60s and are more concerned than ever about retirement. They know they need to save, but how much? And what exactly are they saving for—to spend more time 36 the grandkids, go traveling, or start another career? It turns out that husbands and wives may have 37 different ideas about the subject.

The deepest divide is in the way spouses envisage their lifestyle in their later years. Fidelity Investments Inc. found 41 percent of the 500 couples it surveyed 38 on whether both or at least one spouse will work in retirement. Wives are generally right regarding their husbands’ retirement age, but men 39 the age their wives will be when they stop working. And husbands are slightly more 40 about their standard of living than wives are.

Busy juggling (穷于应付)careers and families, most couples don’t take the time to sit down, 41 or together, and think about what they would like to do 5, 10 or 20 years from now. They 42 they are on the same page, but the 43 is they have avoided even talking about it.

If you are self-employed or in a job that doesn’t have a standard retirement age, you may be more apt to delay thinking about these issues, It is often a 44 retirement date that provides the catalyst (催化剂）to start planning. Getting laid off or accepting an early-retirement 45 can force your hand. But don’t wait until you get a severance (遣散费）check to begin planning. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。

paragraphs.sourceText: What If Middle-Class Jobs Disappear?
paragraphs.translationZh: 如果中产阶级工作消失怎么办？

paragraphs.sourceText: A) The most recent recession in the United States began in December 2007 and ended in June 2009, according to the National Bureau of Economic Research. However, two years after the official end of the recession, few Americans would say that economic troubles are behind us. The unemployment rate, in particular, remains above 9%. Some labor market indicators, such as the proportion of long-term unemployed, are worse now than for any postwar recession.
paragraphs.translationZh: A) 根据美国国家经济研究局的数据，美国最近一次经济衰退始于 2007 年 12 月，结束于 2009 年 6 月。然而，在经济衰退正式结束两年后，很少有美国人会说经济困难已经过去。尤其是失业率仍保持在9%以上。一些劳动力市场指标，例如长期失业者的比例，现在比战后任何一次衰退都要糟糕。

paragraphs.sourceText: B) There are two widely circulated narratives to explain what’s going on. The Keynesian narrative is that there has been a major drop in aggregate demand. According to this narrative, the slump can be largely cured by using monetary and fiscal (财政的） stimulus. The main anti-Keynesian narrative is that businesses are suffering from uncertainty and over-regulation. According to this narrative, the slump can be cured by having the government commit to and follow a more hands-off approach.
paragraphs.translationZh: B）有两种广泛流传的说法可以解释正在发生的事情。凯恩斯主义的说法是总需求大幅下降。根据这种叙述，经济衰退在很大程度上可以通过货币和财政刺激来治愈。主要的反凯恩斯主义叙述是企业正遭受不确定性和过度监管。根据这种叙述，经济衰退可以通过让政府承诺并遵循更加不干涉的方式来治愈。

paragraphs.sourceText: C) I want to suggest a third interpretation. Without ruling out a role for aggregate demand or for the regulatory environment, I wish to suggest that structural change is an important factor in the current rate of high unemployment. The economy is in a state of transition, in which the middle-class jobs that emerged after World War Ⅱhave begun to decline. As Erik Brynjolfsson and Andrew McAfee put it in a recent e-book Race Against the Machine : “The root of our problems is not that we’re in a great recession, or a great stagnation (停滞）,but rather that we are in the early throes(阵痛）of a great restructuring. ’’
paragraphs.translationZh: C) 我想提出第三种解释。在不排除总需求或监管环境的作用的情况下，我想指出结构性变化是当前高失业率的一个重要因素。经济正处于转型状态，二战后出现的中产阶级就业岗位开始减少。正如埃里克·布林约尔松 (Erik Brynjolfsson) 和安德鲁·麦卡菲 (Andrew McAfee) 在最近的一本电子书《与机器竞赛》中所说：“我们问题的根源不是我们正处于一场大衰退或大停滞（劳动力）中，而是我们正处于一场伟大重组的早期阵痛中。”

paragraphs.sourceText: D) In fact, I believe the Great Depression of the 1930s can also be interpreted in part as an economic transition. The impact of the internal combustion engine (内燃机）and the small electric motor on farming and manufacturing reduced the value of uneducated laborers. Instead, by the 1950s, a middle class of largely clerical (从事文秘考必工作的）workers was the most significant part of the labor force. Between 1930 and 1950, the United States economy underwent a great transition. Demand fell for human effort such as lifting, squeezing, and hammering. Demand increased for workers who could read and follow directions. The evolutionary process eventually changed us from a nation of laborers to a nation of clerks.
paragraphs.translationZh: D) 事实上，我认为 20 世纪 30 年代的大萧条也可以部分解释为经济转型。内燃机和小型电动机对农业和制造业的影响降低了未受过教育的劳动力的价值。相反，到了 20 世纪 50 年代，以从事文秘考必工作的）工人为主的中产阶级成为劳动力中最重要的部分。1930 年至 1950 年间，美国经济经历了一次巨大的转型。对诸如举重、挤压和锤击等人力的需求下降。对能够阅读和阅读的工人的需求增加了。进化过程最终使我们从一个劳动者的国家变成了一个职员的国家。

paragraphs.sourceText: E) The proportion of employment classified as “clerical workers” grew from 5.2% in 1910 to a peak of 19.3% in 1980. (However, by 2000 this proportion had edged down to 17. 4%.) Overall, workers classified as clerical workers, technical workers, managers and officials exceeded 50% of the labor force by 2000. Corresponding declines took place in the manual occupations. Workers classified as laborers, other than farm hands or miners, peaked at 11. 4% of the labor force in 1920 but were barely 6% by 1950 and less than 4% by 2000. Farmers and farm laborers fell from 33% of the labor force in 1910 to less than 15% by 1950 and only 1.2% in 2000.
paragraphs.translationZh: E）“文职人员”的就业比例从 1910 年的 5.2％增长到 1980 年的 19.3％的峰值。（但到 2000 年，这一比例已微降至 17。4％。）总体而言，到 2000 年，文职人员、技术工人、管理人员和官员的就业人数超过了劳动力的 50％。体力职业也相应下降。除农场工人或矿工外，被归类为劳动者的工人在 1920 年达到劳动力人口的 11. 4%，但到 1950 年仅占 6%，到 2000 年不到 4%。农民和农场工人占劳动力的比例从 1910 年的 33% 下降到 1950 年的不到 15%，到 2000 年仅为 1.2%。

paragraphs.sourceText: F) The introduction of the tractor and improvements in the factory rapidly reduced the demand for uneducated workers. By the 1930s, a marginal farm hand could not produce enough to justify his employment. Sharecropping, never much better than a subsistence occupation, was no longer viable（可行的）。Meanwhile, machines were replacing manufacturing occupations like cigar rolling and glass blowing for light bulbs.
paragraphs.translationZh: F）拖拉机的引进和工厂的改进迅速减少了对未受过教育的工人的需求。到了 20 世纪 30 年代，边缘农场工人的产出不足以证明他的就业是合理的。佃农从来都不比自给自足的职业好多少，但它已经不再可行。与此同时，机器正在取代卷雪茄和吹制灯泡玻璃等制造业职业。

paragraphs.sourceText: G) The structural-transition interpretation of the unemployment problem of the 1930s would be that the demand for uneducated workers in the United States had fallen, but the supply remained high. The high school graduation rate was only 8.8% in 1912 and still just 29% in 1931. By 1950, it had reached 59%. With a new generation of workers who had completed high school, the mismatch between skills and jobs had been greatly reduced.
paragraphs.translationZh: G) 对 1930 年代失业问题的结构转型解释是，美国对未受过教育的工人的需求下降了，但供给仍然很高。 1912年高中毕业率仅为8.8%，1931年仍仅为29%。到1950年已达到59%。随着新一代工人完成高中学业，技能与工作之间的不匹配现象已大大减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: H) What took place after World War Ⅱwas not the revival of a 1920s economy, with its small farming units, urban manufacturing, and plurality of laborers. Instead, the 1950s saw the creation of a new suburban economy, with a plurality of white-collar workers. With an expanded transportation and communications infrastructure(基础设施)，businesses needed telephone operators, shipping clerks and similar occupations. If you could read, follow simple instructions, and settle into a routine, you could find a job in the post-war economy.
paragraphs.translationZh: H) 第二次世界大战后发生的事情并不是 20 年代经济的复兴，其农业单位规模较小，城市制造业和劳动力众多。相反，20 世纪 50 年代出现了新的郊区经济，其中白领工人占多数。随着交通和通讯基础设施的扩大，企业需要电话接线员、航运职员和类似的职业。如果你能阅读、遵循简单的指示并养成习惯，你就可以在战后经济中找到一份工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: I) The trend away from manual labor has continued. Even within the manufacturing sector, the share of production and non-supervisory workers in manufacturing employment went from, over 85% just after World WarⅡto less than 70% in more recent years. To put this another way, the proportion of white- collar work in manufacturing has doubled over the past 50 years. On the factory floor itself, work has become less physically demanding. Instead, it requires more cognitive skills and the ability to understand and carry out well-defined procedures.
paragraphs.translationZh: I) 远离体力劳动的趋势仍在继续。即使在制造业内部，生产和非管理工人在制造业就业中的比例也从二战后的85%以上下降到近年来的不足70%。换句话说，过去 50 年来，制造业中白领工作的比例翻了一番。在工厂车间，工作对体力的要求降低了。相反，它需要更多的认知技能以及理解和执行明确定义的程序的能力。

paragraphs.sourceText: J) As noted earlier, the proportion of clerical workers in the economy peaked in 1980. By that date, computers and advanced communications equipment had already begun to affect telephone operations and banking. The rise of the personal computer and the Internet has widened the impact of these technologies to include nearly every business and industry.
paragraphs.translationZh: J) 如前所述，文员在经济中的比例在 1980 年达到顶峰。到那时，计算机和先进的通信设备已经开始影响电话业务和银行业务。个人计算机和互联网的兴起扩大了这些技术的影响范围，几乎涵盖了所有企业和行业。

paragraphs.sourceText: K) The economy today differs from that of a generation ago. Mortgage and consumer loan underwriters (风险评估人）have been replaced by credit scoring. Record stores have been replaced by music downloads. Book stores are closing, while sales of books on electronic readers have increased. Data entry has been moved off shore. Routine customer support also has been outsourced (外包）overseas.
paragraphs.translationZh: K) 今天的经济与上一代人不同。抵押贷款和消费贷款承销商（风险评估人）已被信用评分所取代。唱片店已被音乐下载所取代。书店正在关闭，而电子阅读器上的书籍销量有所增加。数据输入已移至海外。日常客户支持也已外包（外包）海外。

paragraphs.sourceText: L) These trends serve to limit the availability of well-defined jobs. If a job can be characterized by a precise set of instructions, then that job is a candidate to be automated or outsourced to modestly educated workers in developing countries. The result is what David Autor calls the polarization of the American job market.
paragraphs.translationZh: L) 这些趋势限制了明确工作的可用性。如果一项工作可以通过一套精确的指令来表征，那么该工作就可以被自动化或外包给发展中国家受过中等教育的工人。结果就是大卫·奥托所说的美国就业市场的两极分化。

paragraphs.sourceText: M) Using the latest Census Bureau data, Matthew Slaughter found that from 2000 to 2010 the real earnings of college graduates (with no advanced degree) fell by more in percentage terms than the earnings of high school graduates. In fact, over this period the only education category to show an increase in earnings was those with advanced degrees.
paragraphs.translationZh: M) 马修·斯劳特 (Matthew Slaughter) 利用最新的人口普查局数据发现，从 2000 年到 2010 年，大学毕业生（没有高级学位）的实际收入下降百分比高于高中毕业生的收入。事实上，在此期间，唯一显示出收入增长的教育类别是拥有高等学位的教育类别。

paragraphs.sourceText: N) The outlook for mid-skill jobs would not appear to be bright. Communications technology and computer intelligence continue to improve, putting more occupations at risk. For example, many people earn a living as drivers, including trucks and taxicabs. However, the age of driverless vehicles appears to be moving closer. Another example is in the field of education. In the fall of 2011, an experiment with an online course in artificial intelligence conducted by two Stanford professors drew tens of thousands of registrants（报名者）。This increases the student-teacher ratio by a factor of close to a thousand. Imagine the number of teaching jobs that might be eliminated if this could be done for math, economics, chemistry, and so on.
paragraphs.translationZh: N) 中等技能工作的前景似乎并不光明。通信技术和计算机智能不断进步，使更多职业面临风险。例如，许多人以司机为生，包括卡车和出租车。然而，无人驾驶汽车的时代似乎正在临近。另一个例子是在教育领域。 2011年秋天，两位斯坦福大学教授进行的人工智能在线课程实验吸引了数万名报名者。这使学生与教师的比例增加了近千倍。想象一下，如果数学、经济学、化学等学科能够做到这一点，那么可能会减少多少教学工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: O) It’s important to bear in mind that when we offer a structural interpretation of unemployment，a “loss of jobs” means an increase in productivity. Traditionally, economists have argued that productivity increases are a good thing, even though they may cause unemployment for some workers in the short run. In the long run, the economy does not run out of jobs. Rather, new jobs emerge as old jobs disappear. The story we tell is that average well-being rises, and the more people are able to adapt, the more widespread the improvement becomes.
paragraphs.translationZh: O）重要的是要记住，当我们对失业进行结构性解释时，“失业”意味着生产率的提高。传统上，经济学家认为生产率提高是一件好事，尽管短期内可能会导致一些工人失业。从长远来看，经济不会耗尽就业机会。相反，随着旧工作的消失，新工作的出现。我们讲述的故事是，平均幸福感上升，而且越多的人能够适应，改善的范围就越大。

paragraphs.sourceText: 46. Even factory floor work today has become intellectually challenging rather than physically demanding.
paragraphs.translationZh: 46. 即使今天的工厂车间工作也变得对智力具有挑战性，而不是体力要求。

paragraphs.sourceText: 47. Increases in productivity prove beneficial though some people may lose their jobs temporarily.
paragraphs.translationZh: 47. 生产力的提高被证明是有益的，尽管有些人可能会暂时失业。

paragraphs.sourceText: 48. The unemployment rate remained high even two years after the government declared the recent recession was over.
paragraphs.translationZh: 48. 即使在政府宣布最近的经济衰退结束两年后，失业率仍然很高。

paragraphs.sourceText: 49. The author suggests that the recent high unemployment rate is mainly caused by a decrease of middle- class jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 49. 作者认为，近期失业率居高不下的主要原因是中产阶级就业机会减少。

paragraphs.sourceText: 50. The creation of a suburban economy in the 1950s created lots of office jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 50. 20世纪50年代郊区经济的创建创造了大量办公室工作岗位。

paragraphs.sourceText: 51. In the first decade of the 21st century, only people with postgraduate degrees experienced an increase in earnings.
paragraphs.translationZh: 51. 在 21 世纪的第一个十年，只有拥有研究生学位的人才经历了收入的增长。

paragraphs.sourceText: 52. One economics theory suggests using monetary and fiscal stimulus to cope with an economic recession.
paragraphs.translationZh: 52. 一种经济学理论建议利用货币和财政刺激来应对经济衰退。

paragraphs.sourceText: 53. The popularity of online courses may eliminate many teaching jobs.
paragraphs.translationZh: 53. 在线课程的流行可能会消除许多教学工作。

paragraphs.sourceText: 54. Computer technology has brought about revolutionary changes in the record and book business.
paragraphs.translationZh: 54. 计算机技术给唱片和图书行业带来了革命性的变化。

paragraphs.sourceText: 55. White-collar workers accounted for more than half of the labor force by the end of the 20th century.

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 56 to 60 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 56 至 60 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: “Deep reading” —as opposed to the often superficial reading we do on the Web —is an endangered practice, one we ought to take steps to preserve as we would a historic building or a significant work of art. Its disappearance would jeopardize the intellectual and emotional development of generations growing up online, as well as the preservation of a critical part of our culture: the novels, poems and other kinds of literature that can be appreciated only by readers whose brains, quite literally, have been trained to understand them.
paragraphs.translationZh: “深度阅读”——与我们在网络上经常进行的肤浅阅读相反——是一种濒临灭绝的做法，我们应该采取措施保护它，就像保护历史建筑或重要的艺术品一样。它的消失将危及在网上成长的几代人的智力和情感发展，以及我们文化的一个关键部分的保存：小说、诗歌和其他类型的文学作品只能由那些大脑经过训练才能理解的读者欣赏。

paragraphs.sourceText: Recent research in cognitive science and psychology has demonstrated that deep reading —slow, immersive, rich in sensory detail and emotional and moral complexity—is a distinctive experience, different in kind from the mere decoding of words. Although deep reading does not, strictly speaking, require a conventional book, the built-in limits of the printed page are uniquely helpful to the deep reading experience. A book’s lack of hyperlinks(超链接）, for example, frees the reader from making decisions—Should I click on this link or not? —allowing her to remain fully immersed in the narrative.
paragraphs.translationZh: 认知科学和心理学的最新研究表明，深度阅读——缓慢的、身临其境的、丰富的感官细节以及情感和道德的复杂性——是一种独特的体验，与单纯的文字解码不同。尽管严格来说深度阅读不需要传统书籍，但印刷页面的内在限制对深度阅读体验有独特的帮助。例如，一本书缺乏超链接，可以让读者免于做出决定——我应该点击这个链接吗？——让她完全沉浸在叙述中。

paragraphs.sourceText: That immersion is supported by the way the brain handles language rich in detail, indirect reference and figures of speech: by creating a mental representation that draws on the same brain regions that would be active if the scene were unfolding in real life. The emotional situations and moral dilemmas that are the stuff of literature are also vigorous exercise for the brain? propelling us inside the heads of fictional characters and even, studies suggest, increasing our real-life capacity for empathy (认同）。
paragraphs.translationZh: 这种沉浸感是由大脑处理丰富细节的语言、间接引用和修辞手法来支持的：通过创建一种心理表征，利用与现实生活中场景展开时会活跃的相同大脑区域。文学作品中的情感情境和道德困境也是对大脑的剧烈锻炼？推动我们进入虚构人物的头脑，研究表明，甚至可以提高我们现实生活中的同理心（能力）。

paragraphs.sourceText: None of this is likely to happen when we’re browsing through a website. Although we call the activity by the same name, the deep reading of books and the information-driven reading we do on the Web are very different, both in the experience they produce and in the capacities they develop. A growing body of evidence suggests that online reading may be less engaging and less satisfying, even for the “digital natives” to whom it is so familiar. Last month, for example, Britain’s National Literacy Trust released the results of a study of 34 910 young people aged 8 to 16. Researchers reported that 39% of children and teens read daily using electronic devices, but only 28% read printed materials every day. Those who read only onscreen were three times less likely to say they enjoy reading very much and a third less likely to have a favorite book. The study also found that young people who read daily only onscreen were nearly two times less likely to be above-average readers than those who read daily in print or both in print and onscreen. 注意：此部分试题请在答题卡2 上作答。
paragraphs.translationZh: 当我们浏览网站时，这一切都不太可能发生。尽管我们以相同的名称称呼该活动，但书籍的深度阅读和我们在网络上进行的信息驱动的阅读非常不同，无论是在它们产生的体验还是在它们发展的能力方面。越来越多的证据表明，即使对于熟悉在线阅读的“数字原住民”来说，在线阅读的吸引力和满意度也可能较低。例如，上个月，英国国家读写能力信托基金公布了一项针对 34,910 名 8 至 16 岁年轻人的研究结果。研究人员报告称，39% 的儿童和青少年每天使用电子设备阅读，但只有 28% 的人每天阅读印刷材料。那些只在屏幕上阅读的人说自己非常喜欢阅读的可能性要低三倍，拥有最喜欢的书的可能性要低三分之一。研究还发现，每天只在屏幕上阅读的年轻人比每天阅读印刷品或同时阅读印刷品和屏幕的年轻人成为高于平均水平的读者的可能性低近两倍。

paragraphs.sourceText: Questions 61 to 65 are based on the following passage.
paragraphs.translationZh: 第 61 至 65 题基于以下段落。

paragraphs.sourceText: Many current discussions of immigration issues talk about immigrants in general, as if they were abstract people in an abstract world. But the concrete differences between immigrants from different countries affect whether their coming here is good or bad for the American people.
paragraphs.translationZh: 当前许多关于移民问题的讨论都笼统地谈论移民，就好像他们是抽象世界中的抽象人一样。但来自不同国家的移民之间的具体差异影响着他们来到这里对美国人民是好还是坏。

paragraphs.sourceText: The very thought of formulating- immigration laws from the standpoint of what is best for the American people seems to have been forgotten by many who focus on how to solve the problems of illegal immigration .
paragraphs.translationZh: 从对美国人民最有利的角度制定移民法的想法似乎已经被许多关注如何解决非法移民问题的人忘记了。

paragraphs.sourceText: It is hard to look for “ the ideal outcome” on immigration in the abstract. Economics professor Milton Friedman once said, “The best is the enemy of the good,” which to me meant that attempts to achieve an unattainable ideal can prevent us from reaching good outcomes that are possible in practice.
paragraphs.translationZh: 抽象地寻找移民问题的“理想结果”是很困难的。经济学教授米尔顿·弗里德曼（Milton Friedman）曾经说过，“最好的是善的敌人”，对我来说，这意味着试图实现无法实现的理想可能会阻止我们实现实践中可能实现的良好结果。

paragraphs.sourceText: Too much of our current immigration controversy is conducted in terms of abstract ideals, such as “We are a nation of immigrants.” Of course we are a nation of immigrants. But we are also a nation of people who wear shoes. Does it follow that we should admit anybody who wears shoes?
paragraphs.translationZh: 我们当前的太多移民争议都是根据抽象理想来进行的，例如“我们是一个移民国家”。当然，我们是一个移民国家。但我们也是一个穿鞋的民族。这是否意味着我们应该接纳任何穿鞋的人？

paragraphs.sourceText: The immigrants of today are very different from those who arrived here a hundred years ago. Moreover, the society in which they arrive is different. To me, it is better to build a wall around the welfare state than the country.
paragraphs.translationZh: 今天的移民与一百年前到达这里的移民有很大不同。而且，他们所到达的社会是不同的。对我来说，在福利国家周围筑起一堵墙比在国家周围筑起一堵墙更好。

paragraphs.sourceText: But the welfare state is already here —and, far from having a wall built around it, the welfare state is expanding in all directions. We do not have a choice between the welfare state and open borders. Anything we try to do as regards immigration laws has to be done in the context of a huge welfare state that is already a major, inescapable fact of life.
paragraphs.translationZh: 但福利国家已经到来——而且福利国家远没有在其周围筑起围墙，而是正在向各个方向扩张。我们在福利国家和开放边界之间别无选择。我们在移民法方面所做的任何事情都必须在一个巨大的福利国家的背景下进行，这已经是生活中一个重要的、不可避免的事实。

paragraphs.sourceText: Among other facts of life utterly ignored by many advocates of de facto amnesty( 事实上的大救）is that the free international movement of people is different from free international trade in goods.
paragraphs.translationZh: 许多事实上的大赦倡导者完全忽视的生活事实之一是，人员的自由国际流动与货物的自由国际贸易不同。

paragraphs.sourceText: Buying cars or cameras from other countries is not the same as admitting people from those countries or any other countries. Unlike inanimate objects, people have cultures and not all cultures are compatible with the culture in this country that has produced such benefits for the American people for so long.
paragraphs.translationZh: 从其他国家购买汽车或相机并不等同于接纳来自这些国家或任何其他国家的人。与无生命的物体不同，人们有文化，但并非所有文化都与这个国家的文化兼容，这个国家长期以来为美国人民带来了如此多的利益。

paragraphs.sourceText: Not only the United States, but the Western world in general, has been discovering the hard way that admitting people with incompatible cultures is an irreversible decision with incalculable consequences. If we do not see that after recent terrorist attacks on the streets of Boston and London, when will we see it?
paragraphs.translationZh: 不仅是美国，整个西方世界都经历了艰难的过程，发现接纳文化不相容的人是一个不可逆转的决定，会带来无法估量的后果。如果在最近波士顿和伦敦街头发生恐怖袭击之后我们看不到这一点，我们什么时候才能看到呢？

paragraphs.sourceText: “Comprehensive immigration reform” means doing everything all together in a rush, without time to look before we leap, and basing ourselves on abstract notions about abstract people.
paragraphs.translationZh: “全面移民改革”意味着一切都仓促行事，没有时间三思而后行，基于对抽象人的抽象概念。
